doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Father's wedding-party band and starting on trumpet
summary: Ries was a curious child in Michigan; his father worked in a factory and gigged on weekends, taking him along. Ries wanted to play trumpet like him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, this thought occurred to me in the last couple of days because I visited your website and there’s three particular videos that you had up there of varying kinds of music. And then hearing your set, the way you played and your set list. I wondered if, as a child, you were an extraordinarily curious boy?

I was. I grew up in Michigan and my father played the trumpet and my mother played piano. I had three sisters, they all took piano lessons. And it’s funny because my father also worked at a factory, as many people in Michigan did, but on the weekends played gigs. So when I was a little kid he would take me to his gigs, so I was like really small. And I would go and he usually had a band of one or two saxophones in the band, piano and/or accordion, bass, drums, guitar, you know, and so he would sing and play the trumpet. And it was like a band that would play for parties and weddings and stuff like that. So as a little kid, and it was always the weddings and parties I would be part of, you know, because I would always know some other little kids who would be at the party. So I would be there running around but then hearing the band. And of course my dad, I of course loved him dearly, he’s been gone 30 years. But I would sit there at the end of the stage and watch him and look at the saxophones and so I wanted to start playing trumpet like he did. So I started that.
